## About the ML Tag Recommendations Page

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-ml-tag-recommendations-page
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Microsegmentation > Tag Management > About the ML Tag Recommendations Page
- Last modified: 2026-07-10T07:02Z
- Summary: An article about the machine learning (ML) tag recommendations age.

The ML Tag Recommendations show which applications from the Applications Catalog have been detected running on managed resources in the environment. It allows you to review tag recommendations in depth, and accept or ignore them depending on if you want to keep the application tag information accessible for later configuration.

The ML Tag Recommendations page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View machine learning recommendations for matching application tags.
- Compare similar application information.
- Discover insights about collective application data.

## About the ML Tag Recommendations Page

On the ML Tag Recommendations page (Microsegmentation > Tag Management > ML Tag Recommendations), you can do the following:

1. Show or hide the ignored list of ML tag recommendations.
2. Refresh the ML Tag Recommendations page to reflect the most current information.
3. View a list of applied filters. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-tables).
4. Show or hide the filter options.
5. Filter the information by **Application Name** and **Application Category**. After configuring your preferred filters, click the button to apply the filters (e.g., Apply 1 filter, Apply 2 filters) and view the results.
6. View a list of all ML tag recommendations for your organization. For each recommendation, you can see:
  - **Application Name**: The name of the application.
  - **Application Category**: The category type of the application.
  - **Member Count**: How many resources are in the recommendation.
7. Review a recommendation to view its complete information and accept, edit, or ignore it. Any resources that are not selected while accepting the recommendation are considered "ignored." If the user wants to review the previous ignored recommendations, they must check that list. See image.
8. Delete a recommendation.
9. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-tables)
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.
11. View the last time a recommendations check was run, and when the next check is scheduled.
12. View instructions to have Zscaler Support enable or disable ML tag recommendations for your organization.
13. Go to the [Application Catalog](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-application-catalog-microsegmentation) page to view application information.

[Image: A view of the ML Tag Recommendations page and its filters]

[Image: The information details for an individual ML tag recommendation.]

## About My Approvals

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-my-approvals
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Privileged Remote Access Management > Privileged Portals > About My Approvals
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T15:18Z
- Summary: How to manage privileged requests and approvals within a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal.

If an admin has enabled privileged requests and approvals for the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal, a user can access the My Requests and My Approvals pages within the portal. If a user has the My Approvals feature enabled, they can click on the My Approvals icon on the PRA Portal page to manage privileged requests and approvals on the My Requests and My Approvals tabs. The admin must also [configure a portals policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-portals-policies) to enable requesting and reviewing approvals. The My Requests page displays the privileged approval requests that you, as a user, have created. The My Approvals page displays privileged approval requests you have permission to approve and reject. You can view the analytics of the privileged approval requests on the [Requests page](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-requests).

My Approvals provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Create and manage privileged approval requests from the PRA Portal.
- View the status of privileged approval requests.
- Approve and reject privileged approval requests.

## About the My Requests Page

On the My Requests page (PRA Portal > My Approvals icon > My Requests), you can do the following:

1. Click the **Home** icon to go to the PRA Portal home page.
2. Click the**My Files** icon to go to the [My Files](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-pra-file-system) page.
3. Select the listed icons as mentioned in [Accessing a Privileged Remote Access Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-remote-access-portal).
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. The characters & and + cannot be used in the PRA Portal search field.
5. [Create a privileged approval request.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/requesting-approvals-pra-portal)
6. Refresh the table.
7. View a list of the privileged requests. For each request, you can see:
  - **Console**: The privileged console that the privileged approval request is set for.
  - **Microtenant**: The Microtenant associated with the privileged approval request.
  - **Start Date**: The set start time for access to the PRA Portal.
  - **Duration**: The set duration of time for access to the PRA Portal. Access ends after this set time.
  - **Status**: Displays one of the following privileged approval request status types:
    - **Pending**: The privileged approval request is pending.
    - **Approved**: The privileged approval request is approved.
    - **Expired**: The privileged approval request is no longer available.
    - **Rejected**: The privileged approval request was rejected.
8. Delete a privileged request.
9. Adjust the table settings.
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.
11. Go to the My Approvals page to approve or reject privileged approvals.

[Image: My Requests page in the PRA Portal]

## About the My Approvals Page

On the My Approvals page (PRA Portal > My Approvals icon > My Approvals), you can do the following:

1. Click the **Home**icon to go to the PRA Portal home page.
2. Click the **My Files** icon to go to the [My Files](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-pra-file-system) page.
3. Select the listed icons as mentioned in [Accessing a Privileged Remote Access Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-remote-access-portal).
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. The characters & and + cannot be used in the PRA Portal search field.
5. Refresh the table.
6. View a list of the privileged requests. For each request, you can see:
  - **Console**: The privileged console that the privileged approval request is set for.
  - **Requester**: The user who requested the privileged approval.
  - **Microtenant**: The Microtenant associated with the privileged approval request.
  - **Start Date**: The set start time for access to the PRA Portal.
  - **Duration**: The set duration of time for access to the PRA Portal. Access ends after this set time.
  - **Status**: Displays one of the following privileged approval request status types:
    - **Pending**: The privileged approval request is pending.
    - **Approved**: The privileged approval request is approved.
    - **Expired**: The privileged approval request is no longer available.
    - **Rejected**: The privileged approval request was rejected.
7. [Approve the privileged approval request.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/reviewing-privileged-approvals-pra-portal#approve)
8. [Reject the privileged approval request.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/reviewing-privileged-approvals-pra-portal#reject)
9. Adjust the table settings.
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.
11. Go to the My Requests page to manage your privileged approval requests.

[Image: My Approvals page in the PRA Portal]

## About Network Connector Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connector-groups
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > Network Connector Management > Network Connector Groups > About Network Connector Groups
- Last modified: 2026-06-10T14:52Z
- Summary: Information on Network Connector groups and the Network Connector Groups page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Each [Network Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connectors) is mapped to one Network Connector group. A [Network segment](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-segments) is then mapped to one or multiple Network Connector groups for traffic forwarding. Ensure that your Network Connector is up and running for the Network Connector group to be active.

Network Connector groups provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Access the destination networks in the Network segment policy.
- Add a Network Connector to a group.

## About the Network Connector Groups Page

On the Network Connector Groups page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Component > Network Connector Groups), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Select a [version profile](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-network-version-profile) of the Network Connector group.
4. View the Network Connector groups as a table.
5. View the Network Connector groups in a map.
6. Refresh the Network Connector Groups page to reflect the most current information.
7. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
8. View a list of all Network Connector groups that are configured for your organization. For each Network Connector group, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the Network Connector group. When expanded, the following information is displayed depending on the defined Network Connector group:
    - **Persist Local Version Profile**: Indicates whether a Network Connector group is enabled or disabled to persist the local version profile.
    - **Description**: The description of the Network Connector group, if available.
    - **Network Connectors**: The list of deployed Network Connectors that are included in the group.
    - **Location**: The location where the Network Connector group is set up.
    - **Location Coordinates**: The latitude and longitude of the Network Connector group location.
    - **Redundant Mode**: Indicates if redundant mode is enabled or disabled.
  - **Status**: Indicates whether the Network Connector group is enabled or disabled.
  - **Version Profile**: Indicates the version profile of the Network Connector group.
  - **Next Periodic Software Update**: The date and time of the next software update for all the Network Connectors within the group.
  - **Network Connectors**: The number of Network Connectors in the group.
  - **External Routers**: The number of external routers associated with the group.
  - **Advertise LAN Segments Locally**: Displays **Enabled** when the Network segment subnets are advertised to the VPN Service Edge, or displays **Disabled** when Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is enabled for the Network Connector group.
9. Expand the rows in the table to see more information about each Network Connector group.
10. [Edit a configured Network Connector group](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-network-connector-groups).
11. Delete a Network Connector group.
12. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Network Connector Groups page in the Zscaler Admin Console]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-network-connector-provisioning-keys","lastmod":"2026-06-16T07:48Z","nid":"1529077"} -->
## About Network Connector Provisioning Keys

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connector-provisioning-keys
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > Network Connector Management > Network Connector Provisioning Keys > About Network Connector Provisioning Keys
- Last modified: 2026-06-16T07:48Z
- Summary: Information on Network Connector provisioning keys and the Network Connector Provisioning Keys page within the Zscaler Admin Console.

A provisioning key is a text string that is generated when you add a new [Network Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connectors). When deploying a Network Connector, you are prompted to enter this key. The provisioning key functions like an ID for the Network Connector, enabling the Private Access (ZPA) cloud to verify the Network Connector's authenticity and complete the deployment process. Furthermore, each key is associated with a specific [Network Connector group](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connector-groups). The key allows the Private Access cloud to identify the Network Connector group that a Network Connector is associated with.

Provisioning keys should be treated as secrets and properly protected because they can create a resource for a tenant. The provisioning key must also be secured and not transmitted or stored in clear text.

Network Connector provisioning keys provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Identify Network Connectors to a VPN Service Edge.
- Select the signing certificate used to enroll Network Connector certificates.

The following is a Network Connector provisioning key example:

```
1|api.mytest.com|68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2 A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0 AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdb orq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpS ztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ==
```

## About the Network Connector Provisioning Keys Page

On the Network Connector Provisioning Keys page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Component > Network Connector Provisioning Keys), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to show the filters.
3. Refresh the Network Connector Provisioning Keys page to reflect the most current information.
4. Search for a provisioning key by its name.
5. Expand the rows in the table to see more information about each Network Connector provisioning key.
6. View a list of all Network Connector provisioning keys that are configured for your organization. For each Network Connector provisioning key, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the key. When expanded, you can see the Signing Certificate (enrollment certificate) for the provisioning key. Click **Root** to edit the certificate.
  - **Network Connector Group**: The Network Connector group associated with the key.
  - **Provisioning Key**: The key needed to deploy a Network Connector. This entry is blank if you disabled the **View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation** option when [configuring Network Connectors](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-network-connectors).
7. Copy the provisioning key to your clipboard. The **Copy** icon isn't available if you disabled the **View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation** option when [configuring Network Connectors](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-network-connectors). If the provisioning key doesn't appear, and a backup of the provisioning key isn't securely stored in an external credential vault, a new key must be generated. A new provisioning key can be created and attached to the same Network Connector.
8. [Edit a configured Network Connector provisioning key](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-network-connector-provisioning-keys).
9. Delete a Network Connector provisioning key.
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Network Connector Provisioning Keys page in the Zscaler Admin Console]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-network-connectors","lastmod":"2026-06-16T10:06Z","nid":"1529067"} -->
## About Network Connectors

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connectors
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > Network Connector Management > Network Connectors > About Network Connectors
- Last modified: 2026-06-16T10:06Z
- Summary: Information on Network Connectors and the Network Connectors page.

VPN (for Legacy Apps) enables support for legacy applications that require server-to-client traffic using real IP address binding (e.g., VoIP or Active FTP). This service uses [VPN Service Edges](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-vpn-service-edges), Network Connectors, [Network segments](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-segments), and [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/using-zscaler-client-connector). The Network Connector is deployed within your application server's data center, and connects to all known VPN Service Edges. Organizations must configure the route to the client IP pool using the Network Connector's IP address as the next hop.

VPN (for Legacy Apps) connections are only established if each entity (Network Connectors, VPN Service Edges, and Zscaler Client Connector) has the public and private key pairs of the other entities. You can configure a single Network Connector per Network Connector group.

Network Connectors provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Build a secure a tunnel to the VPN (for Legacy Apps) gateway.
- Connect applications as part of a Network Connector group to the VPN Service Edge.

Private Access (ZPA) supports Windows and macOS platforms for VPN (for Legacy Apps). Network Connectors can only be deployed with RHEL9 in the RPM format for Linux.

## About the Network Connectors Page

On the Network Connectors page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Component > Network Connectors), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to show the filters.
3. Refresh the Network Connectors page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. [Add a Network Connector.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-network-connectors)
6. View a list of all deployed Network Connectors. OAuth-enabled Network Connectors are added with a name format of `GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp`. Network Connectors that you've added, but have not deployed, are not listed. View details for each deployed Network Connector.
7. [Edit the configuration of a deployed Network Connector.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-deployed-network-connector)
8. Delete a deployed Network Connector configuration.
9. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Network Connector page in the Zscaler Admin Console]

- **Name**: The name of the Network Connector. When expanded, the following information is displayed depending on the Network Connector:
  - **Description**: The description of the Network Connector, if available.
  - **Network Connector Group**: The Network Connector group that the Network Connector is a member of.
  - **Enrollment Certificate**: The certificate the Network Connector uses for enrollment. You can click the **Edit** icon to edit the properties of the certificate.
  - **Host Platform**: The platform that the Network Connector is deployed on (e.g., Linux).
  - **Host OS**: The run time OS on which the Network Connector is running (e.g., Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9).
  - **Package OS**: The compile time OS on which the RPM binary is packaged (e.g., Linux).
  - **Last Software Update**: The date and time the Network Connector was last updated to a newer software version.
  - **Last Manager Update**: The date and time the Manager software was last updated to a later software version.
  - **Last OS Update**: The date and time the OS was last updated to a later software version.
  - **Public Service Edge**: The Public Service Edge for Private Access that the Network Connector connects to.
  - **Last Connection to Zscaler**: The last time the Network Connector connected to Zscaler.
  - **Last Disconnect from Zscaler:**The last time the Network Connector disconnected from Zscaler.
  - **Location**: The location where the Network Connector group that the Network Connector belongs to is set up.
  - **Public IP**: The public IP address of the Network Connector. Disconnected Network Connectors show the last known public IP address.
  - **Private IP**: The private IP address of the Network Connector. Disconnected Network Connectors show the last known private IP address.
  - **Uptime**: The period of time the Network Connector is available for use. Disconnected Network Connectors are shown as **Not Available**.
  - **Enrollment Time**: The date and time the Network Connector was enrolled.
  - **Operating System Updates**: Indicates whether automatic updates for the OS are enabled or disabled. Automated OS security updates are only available for prebuilt Network Connector images on RHEL 9.x. Network Connectors installed manually using an RPM file on a custom RHEL 9.x build are not supported.
  - **Connection Health**: The health of the Network Connector connection (**Connected**or **Disconnected**).
  - **Secure Shell (SSH)**: Indicates whether the default OS SSH setting is overridden and enabled or disabled.
- **Manager Version**: The current Network Connector Manager software version.
- **Software Version**: The current Network Connector software version.
- **Version Profile**: The version profile applied to the Network Connector. You can hover over the **Information** icon on the version profile type to view a description of the Target Versions for the version profile. If a Custom version profile is configured, you can hover over the Custom link in the table to view details for it.
- **Connection Status**: The status of the Network Connector connection.
- **Upgrade Status**: The status of the Network Connector software update.
- **Status**: Indicates whether the Network Connector is enabled or disabled.
- **Manager Update**: The status of the Network Connector update. You can hover over the **Information**icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.
- **OS Update**: The status of the OS update. You can hover over the **Information**icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the update window and status of the update (**Scheduled**, **Not Scheduled**, **In Progress**, **Success**, or **Failure**).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-network-segments","lastmod":"2026-06-15T13:45Z","nid":"1529078"} -->
## About Network Segments

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-segments
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Configuration > About Network Segments
- Last modified: 2026-06-15T13:45Z
- Summary: Information on the Network Segments page and key configuration options within a Network segment.

A Network segment is a local area network (LAN) IP subnet that is assigned to a [Network Connector group](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-network-connector-groups) to define access to servers that are accessed via the VPN tunnel. Network segments define which traffic flows through the VPN tunnel from [Zscaler Client Connector](https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/using-zscaler-client-connector). Each Network segment has a LAN IP address range for a data center with running servers. You can also assign an FQDN and domain name server to the Network segment. You can create multiple Network segments to define which traffic flows over the VPN tunnel. When you assign a Network segment to a Network Connector group, ensure that the Network Connector and the server associated with the LAN IP address are from the same data center.

Defining your Network segments enables you to:

- Define the traffic flow between Zscaler Client Connector and the server IP address.
- Handle exception traffic for transformation towards Zero Trust access.

## About the Network Segments Page

On the Network Segments page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Component > Network Segments), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Refresh the Network Segments page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. [Add a Network segment.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-network-segments)
6. View a list of all Network segments that were configured for VPN (for Legacy Apps). For each Network segment, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the Network segment.
  - **LAN IP Address/Subnet**: The IP addresses and subnets associated with the Network segment that is assigned to the Network Connector group.
  - **FQDN**: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) assigned to the Network segment.
  - **DNS Server**: The domain name server assigned to the Network segment.
  - **Network Connector Group**: The Network Connector group the Network segment is assigned to.
7. [Edit a Network segment](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-network-segments).
8. Delete a Network segment.
9. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Network Segments page in the Zscaler Admin Console]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-notifications","lastmod":"2026-07-20T09:52Z","nid":"1485436"} -->
## About Notifications

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-notifications
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Notification Management > About Notifications
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T09:52Z
- Summary: Information about notifications and the Notifications page within the Zscaler Admin Console.

Notifications provide information about events related to components, event information (e.g., high CPU), and relevant values associated with the events. Admins subscribe to receive event notifications from the Zscaler Admin Console. An admin can then filter and view notifications on the Notifications page.

Notifications provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Receive notifications from the Zscaler Admin Console about events that are related to components, event information, and relevant values associated with the events.
- Configure events related to component enrollment, component connectivity and upgrades, component usage metrics, system resources, partner federation, and backup configuration.

## About the Notifications Page

On the Notifications page (Administration > Alerts > Notifications), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to show the filters.
3. Refresh the Notifications page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. [Add a new notification.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-notifications)
6. Expand all rows in the table to see more information about each notification.
7. View a list of all notifications that are configured for your organization. For each notification, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the notification.
  - **Component**: The component associated with the notification (i.e., **App Connectors**, **Backup and Restore**, **Cloud Connectors**, **Federation**, **Private Service Edges**, **Private Cloud Controller**, or **Zscaler Client Connector**).
  - **Categories**: The category of the event, including: The text **All**appears in this field if all available categories are selected for the notification.
    - **Backup Configuration**: Events related to configuration backups and backups that are created manually or automatically.
    - **Connectivity and Upgrade**: Events regarding the component connectivity and upgrades.
    - **Enrollment**: Events regarding the component enrollment.
    - **Federated Application Configuration**: Indicates events related to federated application configurations.
    - **Federated Policy Configuration**: Indicates events related to federated policy configurations.
    - **Partner Federation Configuration**: Indicates events related to partner federation configurations.
    - **Usage Metrics**: Events regarding the component usage metrics.
    - **System Resource**: Notifications regarding the component system resources.
  - **Status**: Indicates whether the notification is enabled or disabled.
8. [Modify the display of columns in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/using-tables)
9. [Copy the configuration of a notification](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-notifications#copy) and use it to create a new notification.
10. [Edit an existing notification.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-notifications)
11. Delete a notification. Notifications that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be edited or deleted.
12. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Viewing and managing Notifications on the Notifications page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-pending-requests-partners","lastmod":"2026-07-20T08:51Z","nid":"1540796"} -->
## About Pending Requests for Partners

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-pending-requests-partners
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > B2B Exchange > About Pending Requests for Partners
- Last modified: 2026-07-20T08:51Z
- Summary: Information on pending requests for partners and the Pending Requests page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

For [Business-to-Business (B2B) Federation](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-business-business-federation), a pending request refers to the status of a formal request initiated by a host or guest partner admin to establish a trusted, cross-tenant relationship with a business partner.

Pending requests for partners provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Approve or deny a B2B Federation request.
- Provide granular control over shared resources and user access if approved.

Pending requests streamline the Federation workflow by acting as the intermediate step where:

- The guest partner admin submits a request with relevant details (such as tenant name and token).
- The host partner admin reviews, validates, and either approves or denies the federation request.
- The pending status ensures auditability and security during the decision-making process, avoiding unauthorized or incomplete federations.

After an access token is verified as part of the B2B Federation process, the host and guest partner must approve or deny the pending request on the Pending Requests page. After pending requests are approved, they appear on the [Federated Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-federated-partners) page.

## About the Pending Requests Page

On the Pending Requests page (Infrastructure > B2B Federation > Federation > Partners > Pending Requests), you can do the following:

1. [Add a partner.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-partner-federation)
2. Click the **Filter**icon to display or hide the filters.
3. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. Click **Clear** to clear the applied filters. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
4. View a list of all pending requests. For each pending request, you can see:
  - **Request Date**: The date that the B2B Federation was requested.
  - **Partner**: The name of the B2B partner.
  - **Notes**: Any additional notes for communication between the B2B partners.
  - **Status**: The status of the pending request (i.e., **Token Verified**, **Pending Approval**, **Pending Verification**).
5. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
6. Update the notes of the pending request.
7. Approve or deny a pending request.
8. Cancel a pending request.
9. Display more rows or a different page of the table.
10. Go to the [Federated Partners](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-federated-partners) page to manage federated partners.

[Image: View and manage pending requests]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-policies","lastmod":"2026-06-11T11:20Z","nid":"1483496"} -->
## About Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-policies
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Policies > About Policies
- Last modified: 2026-06-11T11:20Z
- Summary: Information on policies and policy evaluation order for Private Access (ZPA).

Users cannot access any internal applications you've configured for Private Access (ZPA), regardless of whether you [explicitly define your applications](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-application-access#AboutApplicationDefinitions) or [enable application discovery](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-application-discovery), until you configure policies for them. You can configure the following policy types: access policies, client forwarding policies, isolation policies, and timeout policies. If you are using the Log Streaming Service (LSS), you can also configure log streaming policies for information captured by a log receiver. To learn more, see [Configuring a Log Receiver](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-log-receiver#Step2).

Private Access uses the Name Identifier (NameID) within a SAML assertion for [IdP configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-idps) and authentication. Using NameID as a SAML attribute within access and timeout policy rules is not supported.

However, you can use the value associated with NameID within your policy rule criteria by explicitly defining a user attribute (e.g., Email Address, User Name, etc.). In your IdP's SAML assertion, the user attribute can use the same value, and then you can include this attribute in your policy rule criteria.

- See example SAML JSON

Private Access allows you to apply the following policies to your organization:

- Access Policy: Access policy rules enable you to implement role-based access control. This allows you to define rules that determine who has access to an application. To learn more, see [About Access Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-access-policy). To view examples of how an organization can configure access policy rules for a variety of scenarios, see [Access Policy Configuration Examples](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/access-policy-configuration-examples).
- AppProtection Policy: AppProtection policy rules allow you to create rules that define when application requests need to go through an AppProtection control. To learn more, see [About AppProtection Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-appprotection-policy).
- Browser Protection Policy: Browser Protection policy rules allow you to create rules that define Browser Protection requests for Browser Protection profiles. To learn more, see [About Browser Protection Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-browser-protection-policy).
- Client Forwarding Policy: Client forwarding policy rules allow you to create rules that define when application requests are forwarded to Private Access from the Zscaler Client Connector. To learn more, see [About Client Forwarding Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-client-forwarding-policy).
- Isolation Policy: Isolation policy rules allow you to create rules that define what isolation profiles to use or bypass. To learn more, see [About Isolation Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-isolation-policy).
- Privileged Remote Access (PRA) policies: Privileged Remote Access (PRA) policies consist of privileged credentials policies and consoles policies. Privileged credentials policy rules allow you to assign privileged consoles to include designated credentials. To learn more, see [About Privileged Credentials Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-credentials-policy). consoles policy rules allow you to set permissions for File Transfer, Clipboard, and Session Recording features. To learn more, see [About Consoles Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-capabilities-policy).
- Timeout Policy: Timeout policy rules allow you to create granular rules that control authentication timeout and idle connection timeout settings. To learn more, see [About Timeout Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-timeout-policy).
- Redirection Policy: Redirection policy rules allow you to set criteria for preferring Private Service Edges for Private Access over Public Service Edges for Private Access. To learn more, see [About Redirection Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-redirection-policy).

## Policy Evaluation Order

Private Access evaluates policy rules using the most specific application segment and a top-down, first-match principle. For example, when a user requests a specific application, Private Access starts evaluating all of your configured policies, starting with the first rule in a set of policy rules. As soon as it finds a policy that matches the criteria that was specified in a rule, it enforces that policy rule and disregards all other rules that follow, including any potentially conflicting rules.

Private Access evaluates policy rules in the following order:

1. When the application request is received, Private Access first tries to identify the rule that matches the criteria. If application segments are part of the criteria, then Private Access chooses the rule corresponding to the most specific application segment for a given domain name or IP address.
2. Private Access evaluates your policy rules and executes the specified action for the rule. Within a set of policy rules, if none of the policy rules apply then the following applies:

- For access policy, access to the application is implicitly set to Block Access. This is also the case if you do not define any policy rules at all within the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see [About Access Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-access-policy).
- For timeout policy, Private Access applies the default timeout policy rule. To learn more, see [About Timeout Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-timeout-policies).
- For client forwarding policy, access to the application is implicitly set to Forward to Private Access. This is also the case if you do not define any policy rules at all within the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see [About Client Forwarding Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-client-forwarding-policy).
- For isolation policy, Private Access applies the default isolation policy rule. To learn more, see [About Isolation Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-isolation-policy).

These policy evaluation order guidelines apply in the following scenarios:

- Conflicting Access Policy Rules
- Conflicting Access Policy Rules with Segment Groups

- An organization configures an access policy rule that allows all applications for the "Marketing Dept."

See image.

- The organization also configures a policy that denies the "Operations Apps" segment group to the "Marketing Dept."

See image.

In this scenario, even if the organization configured the latter policy denying the "Operations App" segment group to the "Marketing Dept," users from "Marketing Dept" still have access to the "Operations Apps" segment group. When a user from the "Marketing Dept" requests an application from the "Operations App" segment group, Private Access first checks the access policy rules and finds the policy rule allowing Marketing users access to any application. It then applies that access policy rule and immediately stops checking any other policies, because a matching policy was found for the user.

[Image: Add Access Policy with SAML Attributes defined]

[Image: Add Access Policy with Block Access]

- An organization configures an access policy rule that allows access to any application for any user.
- It temporarily wants to block the "Sales" group from accessing any applications, so it configures an additional access policy rule denying them access.

See image.

In this scenario, users in the "Sales" group are not blocked from accessing any applications because these users match the first policy rule, which allows any users access to any applications. Private Access applies that first access policy rule and disregards the second policy rule. To resolve this issue, the order of the access policy rules must be modified so that the policy rule blocking the "Sales" group comes before the policy rule allowing any users access to any applications.

[Image: Access Policy page with rules displayed in table]

```
{
"nameid": "jane.doe@example.com"
"orgid": "86753098675309696"
"saml_attributes": {
    "Group": "ZPA-users",
    "First Name": "Jane",
    "Last Name": "Doe",
    "Email Address": "jane.doe@example.com"
   }
}
```
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Portals Policy

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-portals-policy
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Policies > Privileged Remote Access Policy > About Portals Policy
- Last modified: 2026-06-30T15:02Z
- Summary: Information on portals policy rules in the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) File Transfer System pages.

You can configure rules for a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal with a portals policy. Portals policy rules allow you to delete uploaded files, upload inspected files, upload inspected Internet & SaaS Sandbox files, access uninspected files in the [Privileged Remote Access (PRA) File Transfer System pages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-pra-file-system), and request and review privileged approvals on the [My Approvals and My Requests pages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-my-approvals). Portals policies allow users to access the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) File Transfer System and My Approvals pages in the [PRA Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/accessing-privileged-remote-access-portal) they assign the rule to.

Portals policy rules include the following benefits and enable you to:

- Manage the permissions that provide the ability to upload inspected files, access uninspected files, and request and manage privileged approvals.
- Access the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) File Transfer System and My Approvals feature in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Control the file uploads and privileged approval requests for Privileged Remote Access (PRA).

If you want to configure portals policies, you must first create the [privileged portals](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-portals) that you want to assign control to.

## About the Portals Policy Page

On the Portals Policy page (Policies > Access Control > Clientless > Privileged Remote Access > Portals Policy), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters.** Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Refresh the page to reflect the most current information.
4. [Add a new portals policy rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-portals-policies)
5. View a list of all portals policy rules that were configured. For each rule, you can see:
  1. **Rule Order**: The policy evaluation order number for the rule. ZPA applies policy rules based on the order they are listed here. Change the rule order by clicking on the number and manually entering a new value.
  2. **Name**: The name of the rule. The description is also displayed here, if available.
  3. **Portal Configuration**: The portal configuration you have set for that specific policy rule, with the following options enabled or disabled:
    1. **Delete File**
    2. **Access Uninspected File**
    3. **Upload Inspected Sandbox**
    4. **Upload Inspected Scan**
    5. **Request Approvals**
    6. **Review Approvals**
6. Copy an existing portals policy rule's criteria, and use it to create a new rule.
7. Edit an existing portals policy rule.
8. Delete a portals policy rule.
9. Depending on your Privileged Remote Access (PRA) subscriptions, you will see the following [privileged policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-policy) options:
  1. [Consoles Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-capabilities-policy)
  2. [Privileged Credentials Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-privileged-credentials-policy)
10. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
11. Expand all the displayed rows in the table to see more information about each policy rule.
12. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Portals Policy page within the Zscaler Admin Console]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-private-access-roles","lastmod":"2026-06-09T12:00Z","nid":"1483996"} -->
## About Private Access Roles

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-private-access-roles
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Administration > Admins and Roles > About Private Access Roles
- Last modified: 2026-06-09T12:00Z
- Summary: Information on role management, including predefined and custom roles, within the Zscaler Admin Console.

For each admin, you can choose from one of the following predefined roles:

- **ZPA Administrator**: An admin with this role has read, add, edit, and delete privileges in the Zscaler Admin Console. The default admin account uses this role.
- **ZPA Read Only Administrator**: An admin with this role only has read privileges in the Zscaler Admin Console.

If you are an admin that has ZPA Administrator privileges, you can also create a [custom admin role](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-administrator-roles) for your organization. You can only manage and add custom admin roles with an equal or lower level of privileges than your own. Zscaler recommends that you add roles before adding admins, because you must select a role for each admin that you create.

Roles provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Configure role-based access control using predefined or custom role privileges for admins within your organization.
- Provide admins access to specific features in the Zscaler Admin Console based on assigned roles.
- Manage the predefined or custom role privileges for your organization.

If admin A has ZPA Administrator privileges and performs the following operations on admin B (another user with ZPA Administrator privileges), then all active sessions are revoked for admin B:

- Change the password.
- Disable an admin.
- Enable Force Password Reset.
- Delete an admin.
- Edit an admin's role.

If an admin with ZPA Administrator privileges performs the following operations on themselves, all active sessions excluding the current one are revoked:

- Change the password.
- Edit an admin’s role.

If an admin with ZPA Administrator privileges enables Force Password Reset on themselves, then all active sessions including the current ones are revoked.

Deleting admins with ZPA Administrator or ZPA Read Only Administrator role privileges is not supported for admins with custom roles (i.e., roles with access to specific Private Access features). An admin with a custom role that has fewer privileges cannot delete an admin with a custom role that has greater privileges.

## About the Private Access Page

On the Private Access page (Administration > Admin Management > Role Based Access Control > Private Access), you can do the following:

1. Refresh the Private Access page to reflect the most current information.
2. [Add a new role](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-administrator-roles#add).
3. View a list of all admin roles that are configured for your organization. For each role, you can see: If the permissions for a custom role are missing, you must [edit the custom role](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-administrator-roles#edit) and save the new permissions. A warning icon appears next to the role that indicates when permissions are missing for a custom role.
  - **Name**: The name of the role.
  - **# of Admins with This Role**: The number of admins that are using the role.
  - **# of API Keys with This Role**: The number of API keys that are using the role.
  - **Description**: The description of the role, if available.
4. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
5. [Edit a role](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-administrator-roles#edit).
6. Delete a role.

[Image: Viewing and managing roles]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-private-cloud-controller-groups","lastmod":"2026-07-27T15:29Z","nid":"1507031"} -->
## About Private Cloud Controller Groups

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-private-cloud-controller-groups
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Business Continuity Management > Private Cloud Controller Groups > About Private Cloud Controller Groups
- Last modified: 2026-07-27T15:29Z
- Summary: Information about Private Cloud Controller groups and the Private Cloud Controller Groups page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can create new Private Cloud Controller groups whenever you add a new Private Cloud Controller using a new provisioning key. Every Private Cloud Controller belongs to a specific Private Cloud Controller group, and every Private Cloud Controller group must always be associated with at least one provisioning key to serve any application.

You do not need to create a new Private Cloud Controller group every time you add a Private Cloud Controller. If the Private Cloud Controller group to which you want to add a new Private Cloud Controller already exists, you can assign that Private Cloud Controller to that group. To learn more, see [Configuring Private Cloud Controllers](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-cloud-controllers).

Private Cloud Controller groups provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Deploy Private Cloud Controllers in your tenant using provisioning keys.
- Group Private Cloud Controllers per region or functional area; each Private Cloud Controller must belong to a single group.
- Configure the automated update schedule to an off-hours maintenance window in a region.
- Configure the preferred local version profile for associated Private Cloud Controllers and a Private Cloud Controller's location used in application path selection.

## About the Private Cloud Controller Groups Page

On the Private Cloud Controller Groups page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Business Continuity > Private Cloud Controller Groups), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters**to display the filters.
3. View the Private Cloud Controller groups as a table.
4. View the Private Cloud Controller groups on a map.
5. Refresh the Private Cloud Controller Groups page to reflect the most current information.
6. Select a [version profile](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-version-profile) of the Private Cloud Controller group.
7. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
8. Add a Private Cloud Controller group.
9. View a list of all Private Cloud Controller groups that are configured for your organization. For each Private Cloud Controller group, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the Private Cloud Controller group. Click the name of a Private Cloud Controller group to see its details.
  - **Description**: The description of the Private Cloud Controller group.
  - **Private Cloud Controller Count**: The number of enrolled Private Cloud Controllers associated with this group.
  - **Status**: Indicates whether the Private Cloud Controller group is enabled or disabled.
  - **Version** **Profile**: The profile used to specify an Private Cloud Controller build for the group.
  - **Next Periodic Software Update**: The date and time of the next periodic software update for all of the Private Cloud Controllers within the group.
10. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
11. [Edit the configuration of a Private Cloud Controller group.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-private-cloud-controller-groups)
12. Delete a Private Cloud Controller group. Private Cloud Controller groups that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be edited or deleted. To learn more, see [Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-business-continuity-cloud).
13. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

- **Persist Local Version Profile**: Indicates whether a Private Cloud Controller group is enabled or disabled to persist the local Version Profile.
- **Location**: The location where the Private Cloud Controller group, which the Private Cloud Controller belongs to, is set up.
- **Location Coordinates**: The latitude and longitude of the Private Cloud Controller group location.
- **Private Cloud Controllers**: The list of deployed Private Cloud Controllers that are included in the group.
- **Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys**: The key used to identify the Private Cloud Controller group to which a Private Cloud Controller must deploy.

[Image: Viewing and managing Private Cloud Controller groups]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/zpa/about-private-cloud-controller-provisioning-keys","lastmod":"2026-07-09T12:55Z","nid":"1507086"} -->
## About Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-private-cloud-controller-provisioning-keys
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Business Continuity Management > Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys > About Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys
- Last modified: 2026-07-09T12:55Z
- Summary: Information on Private Cloud Controller provisioning keys and the Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys page.

A provisioning key is a text string that is generated when you add a new Private Cloud Controller. When deploying a Private Cloud Controller, you are prompted to enter this key. The provisioning key functions like an ID for the Private Cloud Controller, enabling the Private Access (ZPA) cloud to verify the Private Cloud Controller's authenticity and complete the deployment process. Furthermore, each key is associated with a specific Private Cloud Controller group, so the key allows the Private Access cloud to identify the Private Cloud Controller group to which a Private Cloud Controller must be deployed.

Provisioning keys should be treated as secrets and properly protected because they can create a resource for a tenant. The provisioning key must also be secured and not transmitted or stored in clear text.

Private Cloud Controller provisioning keys provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Deploy Private Cloud Controllers into an associated Private Cloud Controller group.
- Limit the number of times a key can be used for deployment.
- View the current key utilization count.
- Edit the maximum number of key uses.
- Select the signing certificate used to enroll Private Cloud Controller certificates.

The following example shows a Private Cloud Controller provisioning key:

```
1|api.test.com|68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2 A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0 AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdb orq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpS ztJ/68F0AOEgpcG8McLmwdborq2m6v2A5oNEpSztJ==
```

Provisioning keys are designed to enable auto-scaling so that you can easily deploy additional Private Cloud Controllers and respond optimally to increases in required capacity. When you generate the provisioning key, you can specify the number of times a key can be used to deploy Private Cloud Controllers.

Private Access tracks the number of times a key is used to deploy a Private Cloud Controller and displays it on the Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys page. When a key is used the maximum number of times, you cannot use it to deploy more Private Cloud Controllers. However, you can always edit the maximum number of times a key can be used. You can also associate multiple provisioning keys to a single Private Cloud Controller group.

## About the Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys Page

On the Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Business Continuity > Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Refresh the Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
5. Add a provisioning key.
6. View a list of all provisioning keys. For each key, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the key. Click the name of the key to view the enrollment certificate.
  - **Maximum # of Private Cloud Controllers**: The maximum number of Private Cloud Controllers that can be deployed using the key.
  - **Provisioning Key Utilization Count**: The number of times the provisioning key has been used.
  - **Provisioning Key**: The key needed for deploying a Private Cloud Controller. This entry is blank if you disabled the **View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation** option when [configuring a Private Cloud Controller](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-cloud-controllers).
  - **Private Cloud Controller Group**: The Private Cloud Controller group associated with the key.
7. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
8. Copy the provisioning key to your clipboard. This icon is hidden for security purposes if you disabled the **View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation** option when configuring Private Cloud Controller. If the provisioning key doesn't appear, and a backup of the provisioning key isn't securely stored in an external credential vault, a new key must be generated. A new provisioning key can be created and attached to the same Private Cloud Controller. If the **Provisioning Key Utilization Count** is reached, you cannot copy the key. A **Warning** icon appears next to the disabled **Copy**icon. You can edit the key to raise the limit. When a provisioning key is incorrectly copied, the following error appears in your Private Cloud Controller console when it tries to enroll: `notice:Checking Enrollment notice:No valid certificate. Attempting to enroll notice:Enroll: Connecting to api.test.com via co2br.prod.zpath.net. error:Login request failed - http status(401) nonce(<3|api.private.zscaler.com|0/Z6lDT...>) fingerprint(<oXaN4RRiMc...>) notice:Certificate enrollment failed.`
9. [Edit the provisioning key details.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-private-cloud-controller-provisioning-keys)
10. Delete a provisioning key. If a provisioning key is configured using Zscaler Deception or is managed by Zscaler, then the edit and delete options are unavailable.
11. Download the provisioning key to your system in a text file format. This icon isn't available if you disabled the **View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation** option when [configuring a Private Cloud Controller](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-cloud-controllers).
12. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Viewing and managing Private Cloud Controller provisioning keys]

## About Private Cloud Controllers

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-private-cloud-controllers
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Business Continuity Management > Private Cloud Controllers > About Private Cloud Controllers
- Last modified: 2026-07-27T15:34Z
- Summary: Information about Private Cloud Controllers and the Private Cloud Controllers page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Private Cloud Controllers behave as a per-tenant controller for users, Private Service Edges for Private Access (ZPA), and App Connectors to leverage when the Private Access cloud is not available or reachable.

Private Cloud Controllers provide the following benefits, and perform the following functionalities:

- Downloads and persists a complete copy of customer configuration and policies.
- Distributes customer configuration and policies to onsite Private Service Edges and App Connectors when Business Continuity is enabled.
- Acts as an authentication redirection endpoint when Business Continuity is enabled.
- Allows for log streaming to a SIEM when Business Continuity is enabled.
- Redirects users to Private Service Edges when Business Continuity is enabled.

To provide application access during a global Private Access outage, you must configure, enroll, and maintain Private Cloud Controllers. In addition, to ensure that Business Continuity functions properly, Private Cloud Controllers must run on the same or a later software version as the App Connectors and Private Service Edges. To learn more, see [Configuring Private Cloud Controllers](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-cloud-controllers).

Private Cloud Controller certificate enrollment is valid for one year. To automatically refresh the certificate enrollment, configure the Certificate Renewal Threshold when [adding a Private Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-clouds).

## About the Private Cloud Controllers Page

On the Private Cloud Controllers page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Business Continuity > Private Cloud Controllers), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Refresh the Private Cloud Controller Controllers page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. [Add a Private Cloud Controller.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-cloud-controllers) Private Cloud Controllers that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be configured. To learn more, see [Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-business-continuity-cloud).
6. View a list of deployed Private Cloud Controllers. Private Cloud Controllers that you've added, but have not deployed, are not listed.
  - **Name**: The name of the Private Cloud Controller. OAuth-enabled Private Cloud Controllers are added with a name format of `GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp`. View details for each deployed Private Cloud Controller.
  - **Manager Version**: The version of the current Private Cloud Controller Manager software. To learn more, see [Understanding the Manager Software](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-manager-software).
  - **Software Version**: The current Private Cloud Controller software version.
  - **Version Profile**: The version profile applied to the Private Cloud Controller. You can hover over the **Information** icon to view a description of the **Default**, **Previous Default**, or **New Release** for the version profile. If a **Custom**version profile is configured, you can hover over the **Custom**link to view details for it.
  - **Connection Status**: The status of the Private Cloud Controller connection.
  - **Software Update**: The status of the last Private Cloud Controller software update.
  - **Status**: Indicates whether the Private Cloud Controller is enabled or disabled.
  - **Manager Update**: The status of the Private Cloud Controller update. You can hover over the **Information** icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.
  - **OS Update**: The status of the OS update (**Scheduled**, **Not Scheduled**, **In Progress**, **Success**, or **Failure**). You can hover over the **Information**icon to view more information, such as the update window and status of the update.
7. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
8. [Edit the configuration of a deployed Private Cloud Controller.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-deployed-private-cloud-controller)
9. Delete a deployed Private Cloud Controller. Private Cloud Controllers that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be edited or deleted. To learn more, see [Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-business-continuity-cloud).
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

[Image: Viewing and Managing Private Cloud Controllers]

- **Description**: The description of the Private Cloud Controller, if available.
- **Private Cloud Controller Group**: The Private Cloud Controller group that the Private Cloud Controller is a member of.
- **Enrollment Certificate**: The certificate of the Private Cloud Controller used for enrollment. You can click the **Edit** icon to edit the properties of the certificate.
- **Host Platform**: The platform that the Private Cloud Controller is deployed on (e.g., AWS).
- **Host OS**: The run time OS on which the Private Cloud Controller is running (e.g., RHEL Linux 9).
- **Package OS**: The compile time OS on which the RPM binary is packaged (e.g., Enterprise Linux 9).
- **Last Software Update**: The date and time the Private Cloud Controller was last updated to a later software version.
- **Last Manager Update**: The date and time the Manager software was last updated to a later software version.
- **Last OS Update**: The date and time the OS was last updated to a later software version.
- **Public Service Edge**: The Public Service Edge that the Private Cloud Controller connects to.
- **Last Connection to Zscaler**: The last time the Private Cloud Controller connected to Zscaler.
- **Last Disconnect from Zscaler**: The last time the Private Cloud Controller disconnected from Zscaler.
- **Location**: The location where the Private Cloud Controller group that the Private Cloud Controller belongs to is set up.
- **Public** **IP**: The public IP address of the Private Cloud Controller. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the last known public IP address.
- **Private IP**: The private IP address of the Private Cloud Controller. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the last known private IP address.
- **Uptime**: The period of time the Private Cloud Controller is available for use. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the value **Not Available**.
- **Enrollment Time**: The date and time the Private Cloud Controller was enrolled.
- **Business Continuity SP FQDN**: The Business Continuity Service Provider FQDN.
- **Supporting Files Upgrade Status**: The upgrade status and the current version of the supporting files mapping the Private Cloud Controller public IP address to its registered country.
- **Operating System Updates**: Indicates whether automatic updates for the OS are enabled or disabled. Automated OS security updates are only available for Private Cloud Controller images on RHEL 9.x. Private Cloud Controllers installed manually using an RPM file on a custom RHEL 9.x build are not supported.
- **Connection Health**: The health of the Private Cloud Controller connection (**Connected** or **Disconnected**).
- **Secure Shell (SSH)**: Indicates whether the default OS SSH setting is overridden and enabled or disabled.
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Private Clouds

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/about-private-clouds
- Product: Private Access (ZPA)
- Path: Private Access (ZPA) Help > Business Continuity Management > Private Clouds > About Private Clouds
- Last modified: 2026-07-24T15:42Z
- Summary: Information on Private Clouds and the Private Clouds page in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Private Clouds are a logical grouping of Private Cloud Controller groups, App Connector groups, Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA) groups, and log receivers. [Configuring a Private Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-clouds) is required for uninterrupted access to applications without any manual intervention via [Business Continuity](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-business-continuity).

Private Clouds provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Logically group your Private Cloud Controller groups, App Connector groups, Private Service Edge groups, and log receivers to support Business Continuity for Private Access.
- Configure certificate renewal threshold for enrollment certificates of associated App Connectors, Private Service Edges, and Private Cloud Controllers before expiration.

Private Clouds and App Connectors establish the control channel to Private Cloud Controllers within the same Private Cloud.

## About the Private Clouds Page

On the Private Clouds page (Infrastructure > Private Access > Business Continuity > Private Clouds), you can do the following:

1. View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. Hide the filters on the page by clicking **Hide Filters**. Click **Show Filters** to display the filters.
3. Refresh the Private Clouds page to reflect the most current information.
4. Filter the information that appears in the table. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see [Using Tables](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
5. [Add a Private Cloud.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-clouds) Private Clouds that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be configured. To learn more, see [Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-business-continuity-cloud).
6. View a list of all Private Clouds that are configured for your organization. For each Private Cloud, you can see:
  - **Name**: The name of the Private Cloud. Click the name to view the details for the Private Cloud. View details for each Private Cloud.
  - **Status**: Indicates whether the Private Cloud is enabled or disabled.
  - **Certificate Renewal Threshold**: Specifies the number of days before the certificate expires to automatically renew the enrollment certificate for Private Cloud Controllers, App Connectors, and Private Service Edges. To learn more, see [Configuring Private Clouds](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-private-clouds).
  - **Force Business Continuity Mode**: Indicates whether Force Business Continuity is enabled or disabled.
7. [Modify the columns displayed in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
8. [Edit the configuration of a Private Cloud.](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/editing-private-clouds)
9. Delete a Private Cloud. Private Clouds that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be edited or deleted. To learn more, see [Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-business-continuity-cloud).
10. Display more rows or a different page of the table.

- **Description**: The description of the Private Cloud, if available.
- **Status**: Indicates whether the Private Cloud is enabled or disabled.
- **Public Cloud Reconnect Interval**: The scheduled interval when Business Continuity attempts to switch back to the public cloud.
- **Business Continuity Mode - Start Time**: The date and time when App Connectors and Private Service Edges entered Business Continuity and switched to the Private Cloud.
- **App Connector Groups**: The App Connector groups associated with the Private Cloud.
- **Private Cloud Controller Groups**: The Private Cloud Controller groups associated with the Private Cloud.
- **Private Service Edge Groups**: The Private Service Edge groups associated with the Private Cloud.
- **Log Receivers**: The log receivers associated with the Private Cloud.
